## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Tang Cintāmaṇi-cakra dhāraṇī-sūtra translated by **Yìjìng** ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8), 635–713), the great pilgrim-translator who returned from twenty-five years in India and Śrīvijaya in 695 and led the post-[武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9) Wǔ Zétiān imperial translation programme. The text is one of the four Tang renderings of the *Cintāmaṇi-cakra-dhāraṇī* (cf. [KR6j0287](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0287), [KR6j0289](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0289), [KR6j0290](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0290)).

**Abstract**

The opening situates the discourse at *Khaḍgar-aśrama* (伽栗斯山 = *Khaḍgārya-giri*, "Sword Mountain"), one of the standard mountain-locations of the Avalokiteśvara cycle. Avalokiteśvara approaches the Buddha and discloses his *Wish-Fulfilling Heart Dhāraṇī*. Yìjìng's recension is the most concise of the four Tang versions: a single core dhāraṇī, the recitation procedure, and the salient worldly fruits. The Sanskrit transliteration follows Yìjìng's standard apparatus, which in this period had become highly systematic following his long stay in India. The four Tang Cintāmaṇi-cakra recensions ([KR6j0287](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0287), [KR6j0288](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0288), [KR6j0289](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0289), [KR6j0290](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0290)) are referred to in [KR6j0295](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0295) ([仁岳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BB%81%E5%B2%B3) Rényuè's eleventh-century liturgy) as 凡四本 ("four versions"), and the four are explicitly compared there. CANWWW (T20N1081) cross-references the parallel recensions.
